 StateoftheArt AIBased Speech Enhancement, Audio Denoising, and Forensic Restoration

 Overview

The field of AIdriven speech enhancement has undergone dramatic transformation, with deep learningbased methods now substantially outperforming traditional signal processing approaches. These systems employ sophisticated neural architectures to recover clean speech from noisy, degraded, or forensicallychallenged recordings. The research landscape is anchored by two primary benchmarking frameworks—the VoiceBank+DEMAND and DNS Challenge datasets—along with standardized evaluation metrics including PESQ (Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality) and STOI (ShortTime Objective Intelligibility).

 Current StateoftheArt Architectures

 TransformerBased and Conformer Models

Zipformer represents a major architectural advancement in sequence modeling for audio tasks, introducing a UNetlike downsampled encoder structure where intermediate stacks operate at multiple frame rates (50Hz, 25Hz, 12.5Hz, 6.25Hz, 12.5Hz, and 25Hz) rather than constant frame rates. The architecture incorporates innovative components including BiasNorm normalization to retain length information and novel activation functions (SwooshR and SwooshL) that outperform traditional Swish activations by maintaining nonvanishing slopes for negative inputs. Zipformer also introduced ScaledAdam, an optimizer that scales gradient updates by tensor scale, enabling faster convergence than standard Adam.[1][2]

ZipEnhancer extends this principle specifically for monaural speech enhancement, achieving stateoftheart PESQ scores of 3.69 on DNS 2020 Challenge and 3.63 on VoiceBank+DEMAND with only 2.04M parameters and 62.41G FLOPS, demonstrating exceptional parameter efficiency.[3]

Conformerbased architectures combine convolution and attention mechanisms, with applications including CMGAN (Conformerbased Metric GAN) achieving PESQ of 3.41 and SSNR of 11.10 dB on VoiceBank+DEMAND.[4]

Mambabased models like MambaSEUNet leverage statespace models (SSMs) instead of quadraticcomplexity selfattention, achieving PESQ of 3.73 with perceptual contrast stretching on VCTK+DEMAND datasets, offering substantially lower computational complexity than transformer variants.[5]

 MagnitudePhase Joint Estimation

Recent advances recognize that magnitude and phase spectra require complementary treatment. Traditional approaches that enhance only magnitude while reusing noisy phase have inherent upperbound limitations.

MPSENet (MagnitudePhase Speech Enhancement Network) directly denoises both magnitude and phase spectra in parallel through separate decoder branches, achieving PESQ of 3.50 on VoiceBank+DEMAND. The architecture uses:[6]
 Separate magnitude mask decoder with learnable sigmoid activation
 Parallel phase decoder for wrapped phase estimation
 Multilevel losses on magnitude, phase, complex, and timedomain representations
 Codecstyle encoderdecoder architecture with convolutionaugmented transformers

DBTNet (DualBranch with AttentioninAttention Transformer) recovers coarse and finegrained spectral regions through parallel branches, achieving PESQ of 3.31 and STOI of 95.6% with only 2.81M parameters.[7]

EDNet proposes adaptive erasedraw masking that selects between suppression and reconstruction based on local signal features, combined with Phase ShiftInvariant Training (PSIT) that dynamically aligns phases during training while remaining inferencecompatible.[8]

 DiffusionBased Generative Models

Diffusion models for speech enhancement learn to reverse a corruption process by iteratively denoising noisy speech through multiple steps. However, this multistep inference creates a realtime deployment bottleneck.

ROSECD (Robust Onestep Speech Enhancement via Consistency Distillation) addresses this through novel consistency distillation, achieving PESQ up to 3.99 with 54× faster inference than its 30step teacher model through:
 Randomized learning trajectories to prevent trajectory bias
 Joint optimization with timedomain auxiliary losses (PESQ and SISDR)
 Generalization validated on outofdomain TIMIT+NOISE92 and realworld DNS Challenge 2020 recordings[9][10]

MeanFlowSE and COSE employ averagevelocity flow matching for true onestep generation without knowledge distillation, achieving stateoftheart perceptual quality on DNS Challenge blind tests with substantially lower realtime factor (RTF) and model size.[11][12]

GDiffuSE (Guided Diffusion for Speech Enhancement) uses noise model guidance, enabling adaptation to new unknown noise types by training only a compact noise model rather than the full distribution.[13]

 Evaluation Metrics and Benchmarking

 Objective Metrics

PESQ (Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality) remains the dominant referencebased metric with scores ranging from 0.5 to 4.5, where higher values indicate better quality. Recent stateoftheart models achieve PESQ > 3.7, representing substantial improvement from baseline GANbased approaches (2.16–2.28).

STOI (ShortTime Objective Intelligibility) measures speech intelligibility with values from 0 to 1, with baseline noisy speech typically achieving 0.5–0.7 STOI.

DNSMOS P.835 provides nonintrusive (referencefree) speech quality evaluation with three dimensions:[14][15]
 SIG (speech quality) — correlation coefficient 0.94 with human ratings
 BAK (background noise quality) — correlation coefficient 0.98
 OVRL (overall quality) — correlation coefficient 0.98

This metric generalizes well across challenging conditions without requiring reference clean speech, making it essential for realworld forensic applications.

 Benchmark Datasets

VoiceBank+DEMAND combines 11,572 utterances from 28 speakers with DEMAND (Database of Environmental Noises) across multiple SNR conditions (training: 0, 5, 10, 15 dB; testing: 2.5, 7.5, 12.5, 17.5 dB). Crucially, test speakers and many noise types are unseen during training, probing generalization.[16]

DNS Challenge datasets span multiple editions (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023) with 500+ hours of clean speech from 2,150+ speakers, offering diverse acoustic scenarios including phone call conditions.

 Specialized Architectures for Constrained Deployment

LSENet (Lightweight Spectral Enhancement Network) achieves competitive VoiceBank+DEMAND performance with only 39.4k parameters and 237M MACs through groupdilated convolutions and spectralwise attention.

Mobile Audio Streaming Networks (MASnet) optimize for realtime mobile deployment through depthwise and pointwise separable convolutions, achieving substantial FMA/s reduction compared to standard architectures.

Submillisecond latency models for hearables employ minimumphase FIR filters with LSTM backends, achieving 0.32–1.25 ms algorithmic latency for samplebysample processing.[17]

 Audio Forensics and Phone Call Restoration

 Speaker Identification and Verification

DNNbased xvector frameworks extract compact speaker representations by capturing temporal information across framelevel layers (capturing dynamic MFCC characteristics) followed by recordinglevel layers that provide dimension reduction and speaker embeddings typically of size 512.[18]

Forensic Speaker Recognition systems such as ATIS Klarios automate speaker analysis for courtadmissible identification, supporting:
 Automatic speaker categorization from large audio datasets
 Profile database matching across social media and investigative recordings
 Languageindependent processing
 RESTful API integration with legacy systems[19]

 Deepfake Detection and Audio Authentication

Audio Deepfake Verification (ADV) extends beyond binary authenticity detection to identify specific generative methods through Audity, a dualbranch architecture extracting:
 Audio structural features (temporal consistency of speech)
 Generation artifact features (synthetic signatures)[20]

Evaluations across synthetic and commercial deepfake systems achieve strong performance in openset source attribution, with models simultaneously performing well in both verification and detection tasks.

ENF (Electric Network Frequency) analysis examines subtle background hums from power grids to confirm authenticity and establish recording location consistency, complementing spectral analysis and voice biometrics.

 Phone Call Restoration

Phone call restoration presents unique challenges due to:
 Narrowband frequency characteristics (typically 300–3400 Hz for traditional telephony)
 Specific compression artifacts and channel degradation
 Noncooperative speakers in forensic scenarios
 Multiple competing noise sources and speech distortion

Modern enhancement systems address these through:

Personalized Speech Enhancement with speaker embeddings that leverage target speaker information to suppress interfering speakers, particularly relevant for multispeaker forensic recordings.

Bandwidth extension models recover lost highfrequency content (> 3.4 kHz), improving intelligibility and speaker verification accuracy beyond inherent phone call limitations.

Joint denoising and dereverberation handles both additive noise and room reflections common in covert or compromised phone recording scenarios.

 Loss Functions and Training Strategies

 MetricDriven Optimization

MetricGAN+ revolutionized speech enhancement by replacing traditional L1/L2 losses with a metric discriminator that directly estimates continuous evaluation scores (PESQ, STOI), transforming discriminator training from binary (real/fake) to regression on metric values. Experimental results showed MetricGAN+ achieves PESQ of 3.15, a 0.3point improvement over the original MetricGAN.[21]

QualityNet learns a differentiable PESQ surrogate through framelevel assessment with frame constraints and careful initialization of forget gate biases, achieving correlation of 0.9 with actual PESQ scores.

 MultiLevel Losses

Stateoftheart models employ joint optimization across multiple domains:
 Timedomain waveform MSE for fidelity
 Frequencydomain magnitude loss (typically L1) for spectral accuracy
 Phaserelated losses including group delay and angular frequency components
 Adversarial losses from metric or perceptual discriminators
 Perceptual losses from pretrained speech foundation models (WavLM, wav2vec)

 MagnitudePhase Compensation Tradeoff

Recent research reveals an implicit compensation mechanism between magnitude and phase estimation. When optimizing complexdomain loss, the network trades magnitude fidelity for phase compensation, resulting in inaccurate magnitude but improved timedomain signal. Conversely, magnitudespecific losses improve PESQ and SISNR but may degrade phase accuracy. Advanced approaches:[22]

 Define separate magnitude masking vs. phase estimation targets
 Use Phase ShiftInvariant Training to align phases during training
 Apply silencegenerating phase (CIP) to noisedominated timefrequency regions
 Employ iterative phase reconstruction algorithms guided by DNN estimates

 RealTime Performance and Latency Considerations

 Computational Requirements

Stateoftheart models balance performance and deployment feasibility:
 PESQ 3.7+ models typically require 0.8–62G FLOPS
 Parameter counts range from 0.1M (ultralightweight) to 50M+ (highcapacity)
 Realtime factor (RTF) for CPU inference ranges from 0.01 to 0.5 depending on architecture

Onestep diffusion models achieve RTF of ~0.001 (1000× faster than realtime) compared to 0.01–0.1 for multistep diffusion approaches.

 Edge Deployment

Hearing aids, smart speakers, and mobile applications require:
 Sub25ms latency for psychological acceptability
 Power consumption < 100mW for wireless earbuds
 Model size < 10MB for ondevice storage
 Causal (lookaheadfree) processing for realtime streaming

Recent lightweight models (CRNN with pruning/quantization, EffiFusionGAN, ULUNAS) achieve PESQ 3.3–3.4 on DNS datasets while maintaining these constraints.

 Recent Advances (2024–2025)

Spiking Neural Networks combined with transformers model speech enhancement through spikebased attention mechanisms, capturing temporal patterns with reduced power consumption.

StateSpace Models (Mamba) replace transformer attention with linearcomplexity sequence modeling, enabling efficient longsequence processing without quadratic complexity penalties.

Generalized Enhancement Frameworks like URGENT Challenge explore multitask enhancement covering denoising, dereverberation, bandwidth extension, and source separation, moving beyond noiseonly denoising.

SelfSupervised Learning Integration leverages pretrained speech foundation models (wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, WavLM) as perceptual guidance or feature extractors, improving outofdomain generalization.

 Limitations and Open Challenges

Despite substantial progress, significant challenges remain:

 PESQ overfitting: Models optimized exclusively for PESQ may introduce artifacts, achieving PESQ 3.8+ while scoring poorly in listening tests (the "PESQetarian" paradox)[23]
 Generalization gaps: Performance degrades substantially on unseen noise types, acoustic environments, and speaker characteristics
 Multispeaker scenarios: Dereverberation and separation remain challenging in highly reverberant or overlapping speech conditions
 Realworld deployment: Distribution shifts between clean training data and messy forensic recordings limit practical applicability
 Phase modeling: Despite improvements, phase estimation remains fundamentally difficult, with theoretical and practical limits in harmonic vs. nonharmonic contexts

 Conclusion

Contemporary AIdriven speech enhancement represents a mature field where transformerbased and diffusionbased approaches achieve perceptual quality metrics approaching or exceeding humanrated scores. For audio forensics and phone call restoration specifically, the combination of:
 Personalized enhancement with speaker embeddings
 Bandwidth extension and multirate processing
 Magnitudephase joint optimization
 Nonintrusive evaluation metrics (DNSMOS P.835)
 Deepfake detection through dualbranch artifact analysis
 Realtime onestep models (ROSECD, MeanFlowSE) for immediate analysis

...enables courtadmissible audio restoration while maintaining forensic integrity and chainofcustody documentation. The field continues evolving toward universal, robust enhancement spanning diverse distortion types with minimal false positives or speech artifacts.
